audit.why: 49.59% over 246 games — a near-even lane with a slight Gwen edge.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Gwen four stages and Ambessa none, while the prose calls level 6 'the equalizer' and first item 'the real favor window'. Level 3 was marked Gwen even though whys[2] literally says 'it's a skill matchup'.
audit.why: At 49.59% neither player should own the chart. Ambessa's two owned stages are exactly the ones her prose names: 6 (Public Execution) and first item (Eclipse plus rank-5 Q). Gwen's are the levels where Snip Snip's short cooldown out-chips a comboless Ambessa, and two items where true damage and refunded dashes take over.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Gwen / Skill / Gwen / Ambessa / Ambessa / Gwen in both layers — Ambessa 2, Gwen 3, Skill 2. Difficulty is a mid-lane spike window inside a lane that starts and ends against you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike was justified by 'R's armor pen makes it bite even as she buys MR'. Public Execution has no penetration in Riot's text, and against a champion whose scaling damage is magic and true, armour penetration would be irrelevant anyway.
audit.why: Ambessa's real spike shape here is level 6 (Public Execution, 130s at rank 1, 1250-unit blink) and Eclipse plus the level 9 Q max dropping Cunning Sweep to 10s. Gwen's is Snip Snip ranking from 6.5s down to 3.5s and her second AP item.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten with the real numbers, and the first-item spike re-anchored on Grievous Wounds against A Thousand Cuts instead of on penetration.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hallowed Mist is described as untargetability that makes your follow-up 'hit nothing' — and the page then contradicts itself one field later by noting that R works 'since you're already inside it'. Riot's text: 'Gwen summons mist that protects her from enemies outside of it. She can only be targeted by enemies who enter the mist.' It is a positional shield, not an untargetability window. A melee champion who has committed is already standing in it.
audit.why: This inverts the entire lane. Advice built on 'bait the mist, then go' tells an Ambessa player to give up every trade Gwen answers with W. The correct read is that Hallowed Mist barely inconveniences a melee all-in — it locks out your jungler and your team, not you — so you walk in and keep hitting. The second missing interaction is Snip Snip: the true damage only applies to units in the CENTRE of the cone, so holding the cone's outer edge downgrades her poke to plain magic damage. And Skip 'n Slash refunds part of its own 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s cooldown whenever she hits something, so her dash does not stay down in a long fight.
audit.corrected: Every 'untargetable' reference rewritten as the positional rule with the instruction to step in. Snip Snip's centre-only true damage added to whys[2], whys[3], early, mid and the Don'ts. Skip 'n Slash's on-hit refund added to whys[6], spikes[3] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading was framed around waiting out Hallowed Mist's cooldown as if it were the gate.
audit.why: The gate is Snip Snip, not the mist. It costs 40 mana and ranks from 6.5s to 3.5s, so it is effectively always available; the mist at 22-18s is the long cooldown, but it is also the one that no longer matters once you step inside. Spacing to the cone's edge is the actual trade skill in this lane.
audit.corrected: early, mid and whys[2]/[3] now key trades to Snip Snip's cooldown and cone geometry rather than to the mist.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, though the full layer's itemization and late-game lines both call anti-heal core — the two layers disagreed.
audit.why: A Thousand Cuts deals bonus magic damage by target health and heals Gwen for a portion of what it does to champions. In an extended melee trade that is a continuous drain off your own health bar, and it is what turns Ambessa's won short trades back to even.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal added to wants.you[2], whys[5], spikes[2].text, mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Critical Don'ts listed 'Fight her in the mist' and 'Extend vs her R resets'. The first is the opposite of correct play, and Needlework's Riot text describes three casts with escalating damage, not resets.
audit.why: Standing outside the mist is what makes it work for her. And the real repeated mistake is eating the centre of Snip Snip's cone when the outer edge costs you only magic damage.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to 'Back out of her mist' and 'Stand in her Q's centre'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Snip Snip's range and the cone's centre-vs-edge split were nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Snip Snip is 450 range against Cunning Sweep's 650, so at level 1 Ambessa can contest last-hits from outside it, and inside a trade the difference between the cone's centre and its edge is the difference between true damage and mitigable magic damage.
audit.corrected: Both added — 450 vs 650 in whys[0], centre-vs-edge in early and dontsFull[2].

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are a knife-fight you don't have to win. Q's cone slow into a Maxim-empowered auto can pin her for a Sundering Slam, but the second you commit she drops Hallowed Mist and goes untargetable, so your follow-up slam and empowered auto hit nothing. Only trade when you've seen Mist on cooldown — bait it, then go. Don't blow your dash chasing her E reposition; last-hit, build Maxim stacks, and respect that she heals and resets the trade off her own Q poke.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are a knife-fight you don't have to win. Q's cone slow into a Maxim-empowered auto can pin her for a Sundering Slam, and if she answers with Hallowed Mist, walk into it — the mist shields her from enemies standing outside, so a melee commit is already past it. What actually hurts is Snip Snip: 450 range, and true damage only down the centre of the cone, so hold its outer edge. Last-hit, build Maxim stacks, and respect that A Thousand Cuts heals her off every hit.

edits.before: Level 6 is the equalizer. Public Execution blinks you behind her and suppresses — and because you land inside Hallowed Mist with her, the mist's untargetability never gets to bail her out. Point it at her, not into the wave. Through 4-5 you're conceding short windows to her Q true damage, so farm toward 6 and the all-in. With Eclipse and your level-9 Q max you get the real favor window: Q-empowered-auto-into-Sundering-Slam halves her while R's healing and W shield keep you topped. Force every fight on her Mist cooldown.
edits.after: Level 6 is the equalizer. Public Execution blinks up to 1250 units and suppresses her, and it drops you inside Hallowed Mist where she is an ordinary target — the mist only locks out enemies who stay outside. Point it at her, not into the wave. Through 4-5 you concede short windows to Snip Snip's centre true damage on a 5s cooldown, so farm toward 6. With Eclipse and your level-9 Q max, Q-empowered-auto-into-Sundering-Slam halves her while Repudiation's shield eats the return. Fight with Grievous Wounds up.

edits.before: Be honest here: Gwen out-scales you. Past two AP items her Q true damage cuts straight through your armor stacking, her E's attack speed kites your dash chains, and Hallowed Mist makes every all-in a coin-flip on whether she's targetable when you land. Your purely physical kit running into her health-and-MR scaling loses extended fights. Win it before then — close the lane on your 6 and Eclipse spikes, take plates and a lead, and let your team deal with the late-game Gwen rather than dueling her solo.
edits.after: Be honest here: Gwen out-scales you. Past two AP items Snip Snip's centre true damage cuts straight through your armour stacking, Skip 'n Slash refunds part of its own cooldown every time she connects so the kite never lapses, and A Thousand Cuts heals her off your health bar. Your purely physical kit loses extended fights. Win it before then — close the lane on your 6 and Eclipse spikes, take plates, keep Grievous Wounds up, and let your team handle late Gwen instead of dueling her.

notes: The Hallowed Mist error is the most consequential thing I have found so far. Riot's text is 'protects her from enemies outside of it. She can only be targeted by enemies who enter the mist' — a positional shield, not untargetability. Every Gwen matchup in the repo that tells a melee champion to bait the mist before committing is giving inverted advice, and it is worth grepping 'untargetable' against 'gwen' across all lanes. Two smaller Ambessa-wide problems recur here: an 'R's armor pen' and 'R's healing' that appear nowhere in Riot's text for Public Execution, which I removed rather than restated. Note also that the kit file flags Hallowed Mist as 'untargetable: dodges timed burst and executes' — that derived flag is what the copy appears to have been written from, and it contradicts the description it sits next to.
